name: google-drive-mcp
description: Google Drive as MCP tools: find files and know where they live and who can see them, organize, transfer, share and follow what changed.
long_description:
A single Go binary that speaks MCP over stdio, on your own machine, against your own Google account. macOS, Windows and Linux, on both architectures each. There is no server to host and no service account.

The bundle does NOT log you in. You need your own Google OAuth client and one login first: create an OAuth 2.0 Client ID of type Desktop app, download the JSON, and pick it during install. Then run `google-drive-mcp login --client-secret <that file>` once from a terminal; the refresh token goes to your OS keyring. The README has the full setup, which needs the Drive API enabled in a Cloud project you own.

The bundle asks for the same settings as a client's configuration file, each off or empty unless you set it. Trash and restore are the default way to remove something: nothing that removes something for good or shares past your organization is registered until you turn on the destructive switch. download_file and upload_file refuse every call until you pick a folder for them.

client_secret.title: OAuth client JSON
client_secret.description: The client_secret JSON you downloaded when you created the Desktop OAuth client. The same file you passed to `google-drive-mcp login`.

profile.title: Profile
profile.description: Which stored login to use. Each profile keeps its own client secret, refresh token and account, so one machine can hold several Google accounts, and each is logged in to with `google-drive-mcp login --profile <name>`. Lower case, digits, - and _. Leave it empty for the default profile.

read_only.title: Read-only
read_only.description: Register only the tools that change nothing in Drive. For Google to refuse a write as well, log in with `google-drive-mcp login --read-only=true`, which asks for read-only scopes; turning writes back on takes another login. While it is on, the destructive switch registers nothing.

enable_destructive.title: Deleting for good, and sharing past your organization
enable_destructive.description: Register the nine tools with no way back: delete_file, empty_trash, delete_drive, delete_revision and delete_comment remove something for good, and share_by_link, share_outside_organization, transfer_ownership and lift_drive_restriction reach past your organization. Each call also needs confirm: true. Off by default. This server asks nobody before a call, so Claude Desktop's approval of each tool is then the only check. It registers nothing while read-only is on, and the four sharing tools only while sharing is all.

sharing.title: Sharing tools
sharing.description: all or off. Leave it empty for all, which registers share_file, unshare_file and resolve_access_request for people and groups inside your organization. off leaves them unregistered, the destructive switch's four sharing tools too, and refuses a move, a copy or a setting change that would let more people reach a file than before.

local_dir.title: Download and upload folder
local_dir.description: The one folder downloads are written to and uploads are read from. Leave it empty and download_file and upload_file refuse every call; reading and writing a file's text works without it.

max_download.title: Largest download
max_download.description: The largest single download, such as 500MB or 2GiB. Leave it empty for 1GiB.

labels.title: Workspace labels
labels.description: Register list_labels and manage_labels. Needs the Drive Labels API enabled in your Cloud project, and a login with `google-drive-mcp login --labels=true`, which asks for its scopes. Off by default.

activity.title: Activity
activity.description: Register list_activity: what happened to a file, or to everything in a folder, and when. Needs the Drive Activity API enabled in your Cloud project, and a login with `google-drive-mcp login --activity=true`, which asks for its scope. Off by default.
